title: RevRec Modeling and Procurement Alignment Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Purpose
---
This playbook defines the revenue recognition (RevRec) modeling conventions and the cross-functional procurement and contracts controls required to ensure timely, auditable revenue and accurate forecasting at Redwood Inference. The goal is a single source of truth that connects contract events, procurement commitments, billing events, and forecast adjustments for monthly close and external reporting.

Scope
---
Applies to: Finance, Legal, Procurement, Revenue Ops, Sales Enablement, and Engineering teams that manage customer contracts, invoicing, and forecasts for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
Excludes: One-off employee reimbursements and petty cash.

High-level principles
---
- Match revenue to performance obligations (ASC 606 / IFRS 15 principles applied operationally).
- Keep thresholds and judgment consistent across deal classes and materiality bands.
- Maintain an auditable chain: Contract -> PO/Order -> Delivery Event -> Invoice -> RevRec Journal Entry.
- Minimize manual journal entries via RevRec Engine automation and clear contract metadata.

Definitions and key services
---
- Contract Repository (legal-contracts): Source for signed contracts and implemented clauses.
- Billing Service (billing-api): Issues invoices, posts to AR, and emits invoice events to RevRec Engine.
- RevRec Engine (revrec-service): Calculates period allocations and posts journal entries to ERP (NetSuite).
- Procure-to-Pay Portal (P2P): Tracks supplier commitments and internal purchasing.
- Forecasting Model (FP&A model v3): Driver-based model used for monthly and quarterly forecasts.

Revenue recognition triggers mapping (table)
---
| Contract Type | Trigger Event | Evidence | RevRec Treatment | Typical Account |
|--------------|---------------|----------|------------------|-----------------|
| Hosted API (usage) | Invoice for usage period (EOM) | billing-api invoice with usage file | Recognize ratably over usage period; variable consideration estimates applied | Revenue - Hosted API |
| Dedicated (reserved) | Customer lease/commencement date + provisioning complete | Provisioning completion event from runtime-orch | Recognize revenue monthly over committed term (straight-line) | Revenue - Dedicated |
| Private (annual license + support) | Delivery of customer artifacts + acceptance | Acceptance sign-off in legal-contracts | Allocate between license (deferred) and support (recognize ratably) | Revenue - License, Revenue - Support |
| Implementation services | Milestone acceptance | Signed milestone completion document | Recognize on milestone (over time or point-in-time per SOW) | Revenue - Services |

Procurement & contract controls that affect RevRec
---
1) Purchase order (PO) and contract linkage
   - All third-party vendor spends > $10k require an approved PO in P2P and linkage to the procurement category. PO creation must record: project code, cost center, expected P&L impact, and contract_id.
2) Customer contract metadata requirements (Legal team checklist)
   - Every customer contract must include explicit: start_date, service_type (hosted|dedicated|private), billing_frequency, renewal_terms, termination_rights, acceptance_criteria, performance_obligations table.
   - Missing fields trigger a "contract-data-complete" task in the Contract Repository assigned to Revenue Ops. SLA: completed within 3 business days.
3) Change orders and amendments
   - All amendments must reference original contract_id and include effective_date and accounting impact summary. Revenue Ops approves accounting treatment before amendment execution if the change alters timing/amount > $50k.

Quarterly forecasting and RevRec model (operational steps)
---
1) Data ingestion (day 1 of close window)
   - Billing exports (billing-api) and Contract Registry snapshot (legal-contracts) are ingested into the FP&A model via revrec-service ETL.
2) Driver reconciliation (day 2–3)
   - Forecast team reconciles usage drivers (tokens/hour, average sequence length, concurrency) against runtime usage telemetry. Variance > 10% triggers deep-dive.
3) Adjustments and management review (day 4–6)
   - Apply contract-specific adjustments (credits, disputed invoices, churned accounts) with approval notes. Finance publishes adjusted revenue drivers to Sales Leaders for sign-off.
4) Lock and publish (day 7)
   - Close forecast, push journal entries to NetSuite via revrec-service, and issue internal P&L package.

Specific thresholds and materiality rules
---
- Journal entry automation: RevRec Engine will auto-post for contract-level ARR < $100k annually; manual review required for ARR >= $100k.
- Material contract review: Legal + Finance review required if total contract value (TCV) >= $250k or contains non-standard clauses.
- Billing dispute SLA: Billing Ops must acknowledge disputes within 48 hours and resolve or escalate within 10 business days.

Contract intake and approval workflow (numbered checklist)
---
1. Sales creates preliminary order in CRM and attaches proposed SOW.
2. Sales Ops routes draft to Legal via legal-contracts with tag: accounting-review.
3. Finance (Revenue Ops) reviews and confirms accounting tags within 2 business days; requested modifications are tracked.
4. Legal negotiates and returns final signed contract; contract_id generated and synced to Billing Service and RevRec Engine.
5. Billing issues first invoice per contract terms and posts invoice event to revrec-service.

Example contract metadata JSON (for automation)
---
{"contract_id": "C-2025-0142", "start_date": "2025-03-01", "end_date": "2026-02-28", "service_type": "dedicated", "billing_frequency": "monthly", "total_contract_value": "360000", "performance_obligations": ["reserved_capacity:monthly"], "accounting_treatment": "straight-line"}

(Automation note: the above sample JSON is stored as a string in the Contract Repository and parsed by revrec-service during ingestion.)

Billing adjustments, credits, and cancellations (procedures)
---
- Credits: All credits must be supported by an approved Credit Memo in billing-api and reference original invoice_id. Credits > $25k require Controller approval.
- Cancellations: If termination is effective mid-billing cycle, pro-rate revenue and issue credit; RevRec Engine generates reversal journal entry with memo.
- Retroactive pricing changes: Treat as an adjustment period; document reason and accounting rationale; if > $100k cumulative impact, disclose in monthly close memo.

RACI and ownership
---
- Finance (Revenue Ops): Owner for RevRec Engine, forecasting model, journal entries, and month-end close.
- Legal: Owner for contract templates, clause governance, and contract metadata completeness.
- Procurement: Owner for PO controls, vendor commitments, and contract supplier classification.
- Billing Ops: Owner for invoice issuance, dispute resolution, and credit memos.
- Engineering/Runtime: Owner for provisioning events and instrumentation that generate delivery evidence.

Monitoring & KPIs
---
- DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) target: <= 45 days for net 30 terms.
- Forecast accuracy: median absolute percentage error (MAPE) <= 6% for Hosted API revenue line.
- RevRec automation coverage: target 85% of revenue recognized via revrec-service by Q3 2025.

Audit readiness checklist
---
- Signed contracts repository fully linked to contract_id and indexed.
- Invoice-to-contract mapping for all invoices > $5k.
- Supporting evidence (provisioning logs, acceptance forms, and usage CSVs) retained for 7 years.
- Control evidence for amendments and approvals retained in the Contract Repository.

Appendix A — Sample journal entry templates
---
- Monthly straight-line recognition (example):
  Dr Deferred Revenue $30,000
  Cr Revenue - Dedicated $30,000

- Usage invoice recognition (example on invoice issuance):
  Dr Accounts Receivable $12,500
  Cr Revenue - Hosted API (estimated variable) $11,875
  Cr Contract Liability (reserve) $625

Frequently asked questions
---
Q: Who approves an amendment that changes timing of revenue?
A: Revenue Ops must approve any amendment that changes timing/amount > $50k; Controller signs off on material accounting judgments.

Q: How are refunds vs credits handled?
A: Refunds create a cash outflow and reverse AR; credits reduce AR or are applied to future invoices depending on customer instruction. All refunds > $5k require Controller approval.
